DDInter1640.mechanism: Coadministration with inhibitors of CYP450 3A4 may increase the plasma concentrations and pharmacologic effects of corticosteroids, which are primarily metabolized by the isoenzyme. The interaction has been reported with potent inhibitors such as clarithromycin, erythromycin, itraconazole, nefazodone, cobicistat, and ritonavir during concomitant use of various corticosteroids, including inhaled, nasal, and ophthalmic formulations. Systemic corticosteroid adverse effects may occur following intensive or long-term continuous ophthalmic corticosteroid therapy. Cushing's syndrome and adrenal insufficiency have been attributed to the interaction.
